characters.name: Ajax the Great, Shield-Bearer of Salamis
characters.description: A towering man of about forty, broad as a door, with a bull neck, heavy brow and close-cropped black hair going grey at the temples. His skin is sun-darkened and scarred across the forearms, his jaw square and shadowed with stubble, his dark eyes slow and grave. He typically wears plain wool tunics, leather straps and a bronze-studded belt, and carries himself with the stiff dignity of a man who dislikes being looked at.
characters.backstory:
Son of Telamon and **greatest wall of the Achaean army**, Ajax held the ships against Hector when everyone else broke. He is slow to speak, quick to feel slights, and proud in a way that curdles when ignored.

He lost the arms of Achilles to Odysseus's silver tongue, and the shame sits in him like a stone. *They never said I was wrong. They just chose someone else.* In the sheltered harbour, with the fleet preparing to sail, he must decide whether to nurse the grievance, forgive, or break. His goal: **to go home with his honour intact**, and to find out what that now means.

characters.name: Ajax the Lesser, Swift Spearman of Locris
characters.description: A lean, wiry man in his early thirties, short and quick, with a sharp fox-like face, a thin scar through one eyebrow, restless pale-grey eyes and tangled sandy hair. He wears a linen corselet, light sandals and a short cloak, and always carries a polished ash spear. His smile is quick and rarely reaches his eyes.
characters.backstory:
Leader of the Locrians and the fastest runner among the Achaeans, he was always **the other Ajax**, the smaller one, the one people mixed up with his towering namesake. He has spent his life proving he was no afterthought.

His pride and temper cost him dearly on the night Troy fell, when he dragged Cassandra from Athena's altar. *It was only a moment. Surely the gods have bigger things to watch.* Now in the harbour, the fleet whispers about the sacrilege, and he must choose between **defiance, atonement or flight**, while a sea he has not yet offended waits outside the breakwater.

characters.name: Ajax Unbroken
characters.description: A tall, heavy-shouldered man in his forties with a weathered face, a grey-streaked beard braided with bronze beads, and tired but steady dark eyes. A pale scar crosses his left palm. He dresses in a simple travelling cloak over a wool tunic, with a sword belt worn loosely, like a man who wants to look less dangerous than he is.
characters.backstory:
In this version of the tale, the Great Ajax did not fall on his sword. The night after the contest for Achilles's arms, **Tecmessa found him at the tent door** and held him until the madness passed. He lived, shamed and sober, and chose to watch the fleet rather than die for his pride.

He sails as a man who got a second chance and doesn't trust it. He wants to **reconcile with Odysseus**, protect his family and his men, and learn whether a man spared from one fate can escape the next.

characters.name: Ajax of the Tide, Harbour Captain
characters.description: A weathered woman or man of about thirty-five, androgynous in build, wiry and tanned, with salt-stiff dark curls, a rope-burned neck and amused hazel eyes. They wear a sleeveless sailor's tunic, a woven sash, sealskin boots and a bronze ring through one ear, and move with the rolling gait of someone more at home on a deck than on land.
characters.backstory:
Named for the heroes by a sailor-mother who thought the name was lucky, this Ajax is no warrior but **the best pilot in the harbour**, hired to guide the fleets out through the shoals. Two famous Ajaxes in port, both with a thundercloud over them, make for a nervous job.

They see the war from the water's edge: the glory is a story, the drowned are real. Their aim is to **get as many ships out alive as possible**, whoever deserves it, and perhaps to find out why gods and men keep mistaking one Ajax for another.

npcs.name: Odysseus
npcs.description: A compact, broad-chested man in his late thirties with curly russet hair, a short reddish beard, a thin old scar on his thigh and shrewd, heavy-lidded blue-grey eyes. He wears a plain travel-stained cloak, a practical tunic and a felt cap, nothing showy, and has a patient, watchful stillness.
npcs.backstory: King of Ithaca and winner of Achilles's arms, he knows exactly what he cost Ajax and does not entirely regret it. He wants **nothing more than to go home**, and fears that every harbour holds one more delay.
npcs.relationships: Rival and reluctant respect with the Great Ajax, uneasy about the Lesser Ajax's sacrilege and what it might bring down on the whole fleet. Friend of Nestor, wary of Calchas. He tries to **broker peace** or stay out of the way, depending on who the protagonist is.

npcs.name: Teucer
npcs.description: A lean, long-armed archer of around thirty with dark wavy hair, a hawk nose, deep-set eyes and a scar on his shoulder from an old arrow wound. He wears a hooded cloak, a leather bracer on his left forearm and carries a quiver and a bow of horn and sinew.
npcs.backstory: Half-brother of the Great Ajax, born to a Trojan princess captive, he has always stood in his brother's shadow as both shield and burden. He is **loyal, anxious and honest**, and fears facing their father Telamon without Ajax at his side.
npcs.relationships: Devoted to the Great Ajax and to Tecmessa, tension with the Atreids who mistrust his mixed blood. He is guarded around the Lesser Ajax, whom he considers a **reckless fool**.

npcs.name: Tecmessa
npcs.description: A woman of about thirty with long dark braids, high cheekbones, tired but proud brown eyes and strong, work-roughened hands. She wears a long, plain, undyed wool dress, a shawl and a small bronze brooch shaped like a shield, and holds a small boy's hand wherever she goes.
npcs.backstory: A Phrygian princess taken as a captive when her city fell, she became Ajax's partner and the mother of his son Eurysaces. She has lost a family once and will not **lose another**.
npcs.relationships: She loves the Great Ajax and fears for him, trusts Teucer, mistrusts Odysseus and the Atreids. She will pull the protagonist aside to ask them to **keep the family from ruin**, and may be a gentle voice of reason.

npcs.name: Cassandra
npcs.description: A young woman of about twenty-two with wild black hair, huge sleepless dark eyes and a thin, pale face with cracked lips. She wears a torn white priestess's gown, bare feet and a faded laurel wreath, and often speaks in a flat, distant voice.
npcs.backstory: Priestess of Apollo and daughter of Priam, she foresaw Troy's fall and was never believed. Dragged from Athena's altar, she now sits among the captives on the harbour steps, **seeing the storms to come** and the dead that are not yet dead.
npcs.relationships: Hates the Lesser Ajax for his crime, and sees a strange doom in the Great Ajax. She is promised to Agamemnon, who ignores her, and she knows Odysseus will survive the longest. She tells the protagonist **truths nobody can bear to believe**.

npcs.name: Nestor
npcs.description: An old man of seventy or more with a cloud of white hair, a long snowy beard, a lined and kindly face and watery, bright blue eyes. He walks with a carved olive staff and wears a worn, fine-woven mantle and a bronze clasp shaped like a horse.
npcs.backstory: King of Pylos and the army's elder counselor, he has talked his way through three generations of war and still believes a long story can solve anything. He is **gently vain and truly wise**, and loves to remember better times.
npcs.relationships: Advisor to Agamemnon and friend of Odysseus. He treats both Ajaxes as fractious boys, and will offer the protagonist **advice wrapped in a long story**. He is eager to sail home quickly, with fair weather.

npcs.name: Melantho the Harbourmaster
npcs.description: A stocky woman in her fifties with cropped iron-grey hair, a sunburned round face, a missing front tooth and sharp black eyes. She wears a leather apron over a salt-stained tunic, with a ring of keys, a tally-board and a wax tablet at her belt.
npcs.backstory: She has run the sheltered harbour for twenty years, through trade, war and refugees, and holds that **a harbour belongs to nobody but the sea**. She keeps order with a ledger and a loud voice, not a spear.
npcs.relationships: Respects Ajax the Pilot as one of her best, irritated by kings who ignore her, and is quietly terrified of the Lesser Ajax's reputation. She controls **which ships leave and when**, and can be a stern ally or an obstacle.

npcs.name: Calchas
npcs.description: A gaunt, stooped man of about fifty with a shaved head, a long pointed nose, hollow cheeks and pale, restless eyes. He wears a stained priest's robe with bird-feather charms and an ash-wood staff, and always has a bundle of knucklebones and entrails at his belt.
npcs.backstory: The army's seer reads omens in birds and sacrifice, and is feared because he is usually right. He is **neither cruel nor kind**, only certain, and his certainty has already ended careers and lives.
npcs.relationships: Advises Agamemnon, distrusted by Odysseus. He warns of Athena's wrath and quietly blames the Lesser Ajax, while the Great Ajax sees him as a **bearer of bad news**. He offers the protagonist a prophecy whose price is high.

characters.backstory:
Named for the heroes by a sailor-mother who thought the name was lucky, this Ajax is no warrior but **the best pilot in the harbour**, hired to guide the fleets out through the shoals. Two famous Ajaxes in port, both with a thundercloud over them, make for a nervous job.

They see the war from the water's edge: the glory is a story, the drowned are real. Their aim is to **get as many ships out alive as possible**, whoever deserves it, and perhaps to find out why gods and men keep mistaking one Ajax for another.

npcs.name: Odysseus
npcs.description: A compact, broad-chested man in his late thirties with curly russet hair, a short reddish beard, a thin old scar on his thigh and shrewd, heavy-lidded blue-grey eyes. He wears a plain travel-stained cloak, a practical tunic and a felt cap, nothing showy, and has a patient, watchful stillness.
npcs.backstory: King of Ithaca and winner of Achilles's arms, he knows exactly what he cost Ajax and does not entirely regret it. He wants **nothing more than to go home**, and fears that every harbour holds one more delay.
npcs.relationships: Rival and reluctant respect with the Great Ajax, uneasy about the Lesser Ajax's sacrilege and what it might bring down on the whole fleet. Friend of Nestor, wary of Calchas. He tries to **broker peace** or stay out of the way, depending on who the protagonist is.

npcs.name: Teucer
npcs.description: A lean, long-armed archer of around thirty with dark wavy hair, a hawk nose, deep-set eyes and a scar on his shoulder from an old arrow wound. He wears a hooded cloak, a leather bracer on his left forearm and carries a quiver and a bow of horn and sinew.
npcs.backstory: Half-brother of the Great Ajax, born to a Trojan princess captive, he has always stood in his brother's shadow as both shield and burden. He is **loyal, anxious and honest**, and fears facing their father Telamon without Ajax at his side.
npcs.relationships: Devoted to the Great Ajax and to Tecmessa, tension with the Atreids who mistrust his mixed blood. He is guarded around the Lesser Ajax, whom he considers a **reckless fool**.

npcs.name: Tecmessa
npcs.description: A woman of about thirty with long dark braids, high cheekbones, tired but proud brown eyes and strong, work-roughened hands. She wears a long, plain, undyed wool dress, a shawl and a small bronze brooch shaped like a shield, and holds a small boy's hand wherever she goes.
npcs.backstory: A Phrygian princess taken as a captive when her city fell, she became Ajax's partner and the mother of his son Eurysaces. She has lost a family once and will not **lose another**.
npcs.relationships: She loves the Great Ajax and fears for him, trusts Teucer, mistrusts Odysseus and the Atreids. She will pull the protagonist aside to ask them to **keep the family from ruin**, and may be a gentle voice of reason.

npcs.name: Cassandra
npcs.description: A young woman of about twenty-two with wild black hair, huge sleepless dark eyes and a thin, pale face with cracked lips. She wears a torn white priestess's gown, bare feet and a faded laurel wreath, and often speaks in a flat, distant voice.
npcs.backstory: Priestess of Apollo and daughter of Priam, she foresaw Troy's fall and was never believed. Dragged from Athena's altar, she now sits among the captives on the harbour steps, **seeing the storms to come** and the dead that are not yet dead.
npcs.relationships: Hates the Lesser Ajax for his crime, and sees a strange doom in the Great Ajax. She is promised to Agamemnon, who ignores her, and she knows Odysseus will survive the longest. She tells the protagonist **truths nobody can bear to believe**.

npcs.name: Nestor
npcs.description: An old man of seventy or more with a cloud of white hair, a long snowy beard, a lined and kindly face and watery, bright blue eyes. He walks with a carved olive staff and wears a worn, fine-woven mantle and a bronze clasp shaped like a horse.
npcs.backstory: King of Pylos and the army's elder counselor, he has talked his way through three generations of war and still believes a long story can solve anything. He is **gently vain and truly wise**, and loves to remember better times.
npcs.relationships: Advisor to Agamemnon and friend of Odysseus. He treats both Ajaxes as fractious boys, and will offer the protagonist **advice wrapped in a long story**. He is eager to sail home quickly, with fair weather.

npcs.name: Melantho the Harbourmaster
npcs.description: A stocky woman in her fifties with cropped iron-grey hair, a sunburned round face, a missing front tooth and sharp black eyes. She wears a leather apron over a salt-stained tunic, with a ring of keys, a tally-board and a wax tablet at her belt.
npcs.backstory: She has run the sheltered harbour for twenty years, through trade, war and refugees, and holds that **a harbour belongs to nobody but the sea**. She keeps order with a ledger and a loud voice, not a spear.
npcs.relationships: Respects Ajax the Pilot as one of her best, irritated by kings who ignore her, and is quietly terrified of the Lesser Ajax's reputation. She controls **which ships leave and when**, and can be a stern ally or an obstacle.

npcs.name: Calchas
npcs.description: A gaunt, stooped man of about fifty with a shaved head, a long pointed nose, hollow cheeks and pale, restless eyes. He wears a stained priest's robe with bird-feather charms and an ash-wood staff, and always has a bundle of knucklebones and entrails at his belt.
npcs.backstory: The army's seer reads omens in birds and sacrifice, and is feared because he is usually right. He is **neither cruel nor kind**, only certain, and his certainty has already ended careers and lives.
npcs.relationships: Advises Agamemnon, distrusted by Odysseus. He warns of Athena's wrath and quietly blames the Lesser Ajax, while the Great Ajax sees him as a **bearer of bad news**. He offers the protagonist a prophecy whose price is high.
